description: Hand-written glossary definitions for the core ideas of AmberX AXF. Everything else in the catalog is generated from what the repo registers (plugins, help, assets, CLI tools, build options, features). Add a term here when a word is used across the system but has no single file that defines it.

terms.summary: A JSON file in the one shared asset@1 format that describes a visible piece of the UI: a theme, layout, menu, toolbar, dialog, button, slider, container or access policy.
terms.detail: Every asset has $axf, type, id, name, version, description, author, tags and data. Engines compile assets into tokens and CSS variables; the UI reads only those tokens, so swapping an asset restyles every app with no code change.

terms.summary: Replacing one asset with another while the app runs (runtime.swap(type, id)); every screen redraws from the new asset's tokens at once.
Code that turns assets into tokens and behaviour; the TypeScript reference engines in framework/core and the Kotlin kernel are the same design, file for file.
terms.detail: Engine outputs are pinned by golden fixtures in framework/spec/fixtures, which are the conformance contract between ports. Change a reference engine, then regenerate the fixtures.

terms.summary: A compiled value (colour, size, spacing, radius, opacity) that engines publish as a CSS variable such as --fx-accent; UI code may use only these, never literal colours or sizes.
The rule that all UI code, handwritten or generated, takes every visual value from asset tokens and uses framework controls; check-theme.mjs and check-controls.mjs fail CI otherwise.
A golden engine output in framework/spec/fixtures that every port must reproduce exactly.
One implementation of the framework for a platform: the web port (TypeScript engines + React) and the Android port (pure-Kotlin kernel + Compose).
The validated project.manifest.json every project has; nothing is loaded or compiled without one.
terms.detail: It names the project (its hub folder), its repo and its shared data paths. Rules live in framework/schemas/project-rules.json and are managed in the Dev Console under Standards.

terms.summary: Copying the framework's core, react, ui and schemas into an app's src/axf at axf init, with hashes in axf.lock.json; change the framework, then re-bake, never the baked copy.
A --switch every build driver accepts (CLI, engine-rpc, console, MCP), defined only in framework/schemas/build-options.json; each sets an asset token and defaults off.
A self-contained folder under apps/console-web/plugins with plugin.json, a web part, an optional server part, help, install and uninstall; it can be removed completely.
terms.detail: Plugins conform to the theme engines, put their settings under Settings › Plugins, keep data in their own dataDir and talk to other plugins only through capability services.

terms.summary: The contract that every plugin installs and uninstalls cleanly: code in its folder, data in its dataDir, every outside mention marked so uninstall --all leaves nothing behind.
A named, versioned service (for example axf.llm@1) one plugin provides and others use, so plugins never depend on each other's folders.
A short title and plain sentence explaining one control, shown in Help mode; every control in the framework chrome, the console and axHub web has one.
A narrated sequence of steps ({ say, target, do }) that highlights real controls one after another; screen intros, Molly's guide and Walkthrough Studio all use it.
A walkthrough generated from a glossary or index entry that shows that one feature working, built on the walkthrough engine.
An ordered set of chapters, each made of glossary entries and demonstrations, that compiles into a narrated walkthrough video and optional documentation.
Where every build is split into steps of 30 minutes or less, each pinned to Fable or Opus; the pending list, build queue and Build manager are views of its store.
The one record of every build in _claude/builds/store.json; every write is versioned in the journal and pushed live to main as a status-only commit.
The exact words that started a build, kept verbatim on the build with when, where and who, and shown first on every view of it.
Urgent, High, Normal or Low (P0–P3) on a build; it orders the agent queue and the merge queue.
The only way a pull request reaches main: ready PRs are stacked, tested once on top of main plus the PRs ahead, and merged without a retest when green.
An axHub call that changes something: it is held, Brett is notified, and it runs after a 90-second countdown unless he taps Deny.
Brett's connector hub at axhub.amberxai.com: one place that links his services, holds shared project files and data, and gates changes through veto calls.
The one look document on axHub every app draws from; any look change in any app applies to all of them.
Where every UI change is submitted with phone and desktop screenshots for Brett's approval; plain screenshots go to its Screenshots tab instead.
A named Claude worker with a persona, budget and card; sessions work as the agent Brett assigns and recurring jobs go to the agent that owns them.
A kind of recurring work (walkthrough videos, site checks, landing builds) with an owning agent and a brief template; agent-job.mjs routes it.
The frame around an app's content; every piece is an asset with its own settings interface, reached by right-click or long-press.
On touch, the first tap on a toolbar button shows what it does and arms it for 3 seconds, the second runs it; mouse and keyboard stay a single click.
The Simple / Basic / Developer / Administrator toolbar on every settings interface that chooses which settings are shown.
One registered thing voice, MCP, CLI and the console can read or change, so every action has the same parity everywhere.
The two models builds run on: Fable for foundation work (schemas, asset types, engines, contracts), Opus for everything else; never Sonnet or Haiku.
This catalog: every plugin, feature, screen, control, setting, command, asset and tool in AmberX AXF, generated from the registries and kept current by every build.
